cells.tense: You are here with the pen, directing what gets set down.
cells.act: care for it with fresh hands and see what it needs
cells.ask: Tend something you're growing — a habit, a plant, a skill — with fresh hands this week, seeing what it needs from you. Don't force it. Let it show you, and give that.
cells.core:
You can tell what to hold and what to set down, and setting it down doesn't dent you. What you are becoming is taking its shape while you stand here, without strain from you. Finished things get released when they're finished. Anyone close can feel that you won't clutch, and it lets them settle too. That steadiness is the shape you're already in.

What keeps it going is upkeep, and upkeep is yours to do. Tend something you're growing — a habit, a plant, a skill — with fresh hands this week, seeing what it needs from you. That shows you the next thing to do, and the next after that. What you're building holds because you gave it real care instead of reaching for something you can't see yet.
cells.sheetLine: You know what to set down, and it doesn't dent you.
cells.place: in what you are already becoming

cells.tense: You will have decided how every part of this turns out before any of it arrives.
cells.act: put the inquiry on paper and follow it
cells.ask: Put onto a page what's actually true of what you're trying to become — what happened, what holds now — with no feeling words. Follow what the page shows. Once, no clock.
cells.core:
You keep pushing to arrive somewhere before it has actually arrived, and the push has begun to cost. You know what the finished thing should look like, so you rehearse it, correct it, brace against a version that isn't due yet. What you are becoming isn't getting room to become — it's being denied in advance, item by item. Anyone watching meets a version of you that's already editing itself.

Go smaller than the pushing. Put onto a page what's actually true of what you're trying to become — what happened, what holds now — with no feeling words in it. The page gives you something to stand on that isn't dread about the outcome. Then do the next thing the page shows, and let that be the whole of the next move.
cells.sheetLine: You're bracing at a version of it that isn't due yet.
cells.place: in what you are already becoming

cells.tense: You were standing at a door that had already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Build one thing with your hands that you want still here next month — the shelf fixed, the bed turned, the habit started. Made to hold. No clock on it.
cells.core:
Where this should be moving, it isn't — you stopped showing up for what you were becoming, and the room has stayed quiet. Some of what you wanted has been left waiting. Nothing gets brought in that could change the shape of things. The strength that used to be there for making things has gone somewhere you can't reach from here.

Begin with what your hands can verify. Build one thing you want still here next month — the shelf fixed, the bed turned, the habit started. Make it with patience and no pushing, and when it holds, look at it holding. One built thing teaches your body that building is still yours. That's the charge; the rest follows from there.
cells.sheetLine: The making has gone quiet, and one built thing can start it.
cells.place: in what you are already becoming

cells.tense: You are steering what's becoming while your hand is off the wheel.
cells.act: learn how it grows by tending it
cells.ask: Learn one new thing about how something you look after actually grows — a plant, a routine, a skill. Stay a beginner with it. Carry what you saw; tell nobody.
cells.core:
Release is already running — you set things down, you let people go, you don't cling to outcomes — and by your own account that's just how it is. The steering is happening without you at the wheel. Asked why you let something go, you reach for circumstance instead of intention. The choice is in your hands and your explanation lives somewhere else.

Go back to tending, and stay a beginner about it. Learn one new thing about how something you look after actually grows — a plant, a routine, a skill. Carry what you saw, tell nobody. That tells you whether the release you practiced is care or just distance. Knowing comes before the claim; that's all the ownership needs.
cells.sheetLine: You set things down well. You don't yet own the setting down.
cells.place: in what you are already becoming
